businessSystemsDesign.definition: Analyzing and redesigning how a business operates so strategy, team and processes actually fit together.
businessSystemsDesign.situation: Your company has grown, but its processes grew along with it almost by accident. No one can say precisely who is responsible for what.
businessSystemsDesign.notIncluded: Day-to-day execution and project steering (see Project Management & Operations).
businessSystemsDesign.result: A clear structure for how the business should operate.
businessSystemsDesign.formats: A standalone project (2–4 weeks) or the foundation for a larger transformation project.
usefulWhen: Your company is growing faster than its processes.
You're taking over an existing team or department.
Different people make similar decisions in different ways.
You're planning a larger structural change.
problems: Unclear responsibilities between team members.
Repeated back-and-forth without a clear decision.
Processes only one person understands.
No overview of how work actually flows.
businessSystemsDesign.doesNotPromise: This service does not promise specific revenue or growth figures. The result is a working structure — not a guaranteed metric.

faq.question: Do I need to abandon my existing processes completely?
faq.answer: No. The starting point is always what already works — we change specifically what doesn't.

faq.question: Who is this service for?
faq.answer: Companies that have grown or changed without their internal structure keeping pace.

faq.question: Do I get written documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. You receive a process map, a target-structure document and a role matrix.

marketingSystems.definition: Building one coherent marketing system out of strategy, customer journey, channels and reporting — instead of separate, disconnected campaigns.
marketingSystems.situation: You're running ads across several channels, but no one can say which channel actually brings in customers.
marketingSystems.notIncluded: Day-to-day execution of individual ad campaigns or graphic production.
marketingSystems.result: Marketing becomes a coordinated and measurable process.
marketingSystems.formats: Standalone project or combined with Premium Websites & Digital Experience.
usefulWhen: You're spending on ads without being able to attribute the effect clearly.
Different channels feel like they belong to different brands.
You're launching a new offer and need a clear marketing structure.
Reporting exists, but no one actually uses it.
problems: Campaigns with no recognizable shared strategy.
No clear customer journey from first contact to close.
Unclear division of roles between channels.
Data that's collected but never analyzed.
marketingSystems.doesNotPromise: This service does not promise specific revenue or growth percentages. It builds the structure that makes marketing measurable in the first place.

faq.question: Do you also execute the ad campaigns?
faq.answer: Day-to-day campaign execution isn't automatically included — I build the structure that you or your team then fill.

faq.question: Do I already need channels like social media or Google Ads?
faq.answer: No. We define the strategy first, then choose the right channels.

faq.question: How is success measured?
faq.answer: Through the reporting structure we define together, matched to your actual goals.

aiAutomation.definition: Targeted automation of recurring manual tasks using AI tools and clearly documented workflows.
aiAutomation.situation: Your team spends hours on repetitive tasks that could technically be automated, but no one has had time to actually do it.
aiAutomation.notIncluded: Building complex custom software from scratch.
aiAutomation.result: Less repetitive manual work and clearer workflows.
aiAutomation.formats: A single automation or ongoing support across several workflows.
usefulWhen: Your team does the same task manually every week.
Data gets copied between tools by hand.
You've heard about AI but don't know where it would actually help.
Errors keep happening from repeated manual steps.
problems: Time-consuming routine tasks with no automation.
Data that has to be moved manually between tools.
Missing documentation of existing workflows.
Uncertainty about which AI tools genuinely fit.
aiAutomation.doesNotPromise: This service does not promise full automation of every process or specific cost savings. Automation happens exactly where it creates real value.

faq.question: Does this replace staff?
faq.answer: No. Repetitive tasks get automated — responsibility and decisions stay with people.

faq.question: Which AI tools do you work with?
faq.answer: The choice depends on your actual needs and the systems already in place.

faq.question: What if an automation doesn't work as intended?
faq.answer: Every automation is documented and tested before it goes into regular use.

projectManagementOperations.definition: The structure that keeps projects planned, coordinated and visibly steered through to completion.
projectManagementOperations.situation: Projects are running, but no one has the full picture. Deadlines slip without anyone noticing in time.
projectManagementOperations.notIncluded: The hands-on execution of the project's underlying work itself (e.g. design or development work).
projectManagementOperations.result: Projects become visible, coordinated and manageable.
projectManagementOperations.formats: Support for a single project or ongoing project steering.
usefulWhen: Several projects are running at once with no shared overview.
Deadlines slip without anyone catching it early.
Communication between team and stakeholders is unclear.
A larger new project is starting and needs structure from day one.
problems: Unclear responsibilities within a project.
Risks identified too late.
No regular communication rhythm within the team.
Progress that no one documents visibly.
projectManagementOperations.doesNotPromise: This service does not take over the hands-on execution of the project's underlying work, and doesn't guarantee fixed completion dates regardless of project scope.

faq.question: Do you also handle the hands-on work, like design or development?
faq.answer: No, that's not automatically included — I coordinate and structure; the hands-on work stays with the people or teams responsible.

faq.question: Does this work for a single, smaller project too?
faq.answer: Yes, the scope is adjusted to the size of the project.

faq.question: How often are there project status updates?
faq.answer: We agree on a fixed communication rhythm together.

premiumWebsitesDigitalExperience.definition: Building a multilingual, accessible website that makes your expertise visible and moves visitors toward a decision.
premiumWebsitesDigitalExperience.situation: Your current website either looks outdated or reads like an interchangeable template — and doesn't explain why someone should work with you specifically.
premiumWebsitesDigitalExperience.notIncluded: Producing all photography or video from scratch (can be added separately).
premiumWebsitesDigitalExperience.result: A website that clearly presents your expertise, builds trust and moves visitors toward contact or purchase.
premiumWebsitesDigitalExperience.formats: Standalone project or combined with Marketing Systems.
usefulWhen: Your website doesn't explain why someone should work with you instead of someone else.
You need a multilingual website for several markets.
The current website looks technically or visually outdated.
You're launching a new offer and need a standalone digital presence.
problems: No clear positioning on the website.
No multilingual structure despite needing several languages.
Weak accessibility for people with disabilities.
A website that's hard to find on Google or in AI-powered search tools.
premiumWebsitesDigitalExperience.doesNotPromise: This service does not promise a specific number of visitors, inquiries or sales. It delivers a website that makes your expertise visible and supports decisions.

faq.question: Do you write the website copy too?
faq.answer: Content and information architecture are part of the service. Base copy can be developed together.

faq.question: Is AI used in development?
faq.answer: AI-assisted development is part of the workflow. I'm personally responsible for strategy, quality and final implementation.

faq.question: What technology is used?
faq.answer: Depending on the project: Next.js, React, Motion and selectively Three.js, among others — technology is a means to an end, not the core of the result.

expertise.heading: A website is also proof of expertise.
expertise.intro: Your website doesn't just show what you offer — it shows how you work. That's why building it combines several layers:
expertise.techNote: Depending on the project, this can include Next.js, React, Motion and selectively Three.js — as implementation tools, not as the actual value of the result.
expertise.aiNote: AI-assisted development is part of the workflow. Responsibility for strategy, quality and final implementation stays with Inna.

items.question: Do I need to choose one service, or can I combine several?
items.answer: You can start with a single service or combine several into one project — depending on where the biggest bottleneck is.

items.question: How does getting started work?
items.answer: We begin with a conversation about your current situation. From there, I propose a scope that fits.

items.question: How long does a typical project take?
items.answer: It depends on scope — from a single automation over a few days to a multi-week systems project.

items.question: Do you work with existing tools and systems?
items.answer: Yes. The starting point is always what's already in place — new tools are added only where they're genuinely needed.

items.question: What languages do you work in?
What happens after the project ends?
items.answer: You receive documentation and a handover so the system keeps running without me. Ongoing support is available if wanted.

hero.headline: Clarity before tools.
hero.intro: The work begins with the business goal and the current process — not with choosing software.

understand.title: Understand
understand.questions: What needs to be achieved, for whom, and under what constraints?
understand.work: Conversations with the relevant people, review of existing documentation, and observation of the current process.
understand.deliverable: A written summary of the starting point and the goals.
understand.involvement: One or two structured conversations, plus access to relevant documentation.

analyze.title: Analyze
analyze.questions: Where exactly does the bottleneck occur, and why doesn't the current process work?
analyze.work: Systematic analysis of process steps, data flows and responsibilities.
analyze.deliverable: A prioritized list of bottlenecks and risks.
analyze.involvement: Follow-up questions to help interpret specific observations.

design.title: Design
design.questions: How should the process work going forward, and in what order will it be implemented?
design.work: Designing the target process, the responsibilities and the technical structure.
design.deliverable: A target-process document with an implementation sequence.
design.involvement: Joint review and sign-off on the design.

implement.title: Implement
implement.questions: How does the design get put into practice, and who does what?
implement.work: Implementing the agreed structure — from project setup to automation — with ongoing coordination.
implement.deliverable: The implemented structure, system or website, including documentation.
implement.involvement: Regular updates and decisions at defined checkpoints.

optimize.title: Optimize
optimize.questions: Is the result working as planned, and where does it need adjustment?
optimize.work: Evaluating results against agreed metrics and making targeted corrections.
optimize.deliverable: A report with results and recommended next steps.
optimize.involvement: Regular exchange on results and priorities.

principles.title: Systems before tools
principles.description: Structure first, then the software that supports it.

principles.title: Technology serves people
principles.description: Tools exist to make work easier — not the other way around.

principles.title: Clear responsibility
principles.description: Every step has one person accountable for it.

principles.title: Measurable decisions
principles.description: Decisions are based on data, not assumptions.

principles.title: Sustainable implementation
principles.description: Solutions that keep working after the project ends.

principles.title: Documentation is part of delivery
principles.description: Without documentation, an implementation isn't finished.

approachPage.formatsText: The approach applies just as well to a single project spanning a few days as to a multi-week systems transformation — the scope adapts to the actual task, not the other way around.
approachPage.collaborationText: A fixed communication rhythm, clear points of contact on both sides, and decisions that get documented rather than just discussed.

faq.question: Do I need to have everything figured out before the first conversation?
faq.answer: No. The first conversation exists specifically to map out the starting point together.

faq.question: What if requirements change during the project?
faq.answer: The target process is jointly reviewed and signed off — changes are made visible, not quietly absorbed.

faq.question: How much time do I need to contribute as a client?
faq.answer: It depends on the phase — most during Understand and Design, least during Implement and Optimize.

faq.question: Does the collaboration end at launch?
faq.answer: Not automatically. The optimize phase can be a one-off or ongoing, matched to your needs.

hero.headline: I do not add more noise. I create structure.
hero.intro: I work at the intersection of business, project management, marketing, e-commerce, digital experience, and AI and automation — and connect these fields into systems that hold up in daily work.
hero.portraitAlt: Inna Talianchuk, Digital Systems Strategist & AI Business Orchestrator

positioning.heading: One discipline alone does not solve a structural problem.
positioning.text: Most bottlenecks appear between disciplines: between strategy and execution, between marketing and process, between a tool and the person responsible for it. That is why I deliberately work across these boundaries.

items.title: Processes come first
items.text: A good tool inside an unclear process only speeds up the chaos. Technology starts to pay off once the underlying process is clear.

items.title: Tools alone are not enough
items.text: Software does not solve a problem that is structural. What matters is how people, responsibilities and data work together.

items.title: Websites are part of the system
items.text: A website convinces only when business value, UX, content and technology are designed together — not as separate trades.

items.title: Implementation must stay understandable
items.text: An implementation the client cannot understand is not a finished implementation. Comprehensibility is part of the result.

chaosHero.tagline: Complexity is inevitable. Chaos is optional.

chapters.title: Complexity
chapters.text: Modern business grows more complex every day. AI, automation, dozens of services, data. They create opportunities — but on their own they make business more complex, not more efficient.

chapters.title: Clarity
chapters.text: My work is not to add new tools. My work is to create a system where everything works together.

chapters.title: Systems
chapters.text: Strategy, marketing, AI, operations. Connected into one workflow. Each part reinforcing the others.

chapters.title: Growth
chapters.text: When the system works, the business grows. Predictably. Sustainably. Without constant firefighting.

chapters.title: Freedom
chapters.text: And you get the one thing that matters most: freedom to focus on what you do best.
